newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France re-routes cargo from lightning-hit jet.
newsitem.headline: Air France re-routes cargo from lightning-hit jet.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it had put contingency plans in place for freight aboard a Boeing 747-400 passenger aircraft hit by lightning earlier on Thursday, which was forced to land at Marseille-Provence Airport.
The 747-400 , which was en route to Paris from Johannesburg when it encountered strong turbulence over the Mediterranean, was currently immobilised at Marseille, an Air France official said.
The flight had been scheduled to arrive at Paris-CDG at 6 a.m. (0500 gmt).

"As soon as the aircraft landed at Marseille the perishable freight stored in the belly-hold, weighing around ten tonnes, was transferred to cold-store facilities on-site," an Air France cargo official told Reuters.
The perishable shipments comprised three pallets of fish as well as part-pallets of live lobsters and meat.
Air France Cargo had taken steps to transport nearly all of the freight aboard the 747-400, between 14 and 15 tonnes in total, by truck from Marseille to Paris.
The shipments are scheduled to arrive in Paris at around 6 a.m. on Friday morning, the official said.

"Given that the freight is palletised, we have been unable to use Air France Europe's scheduled passenger services from Marseille to Paris because the belly-hold of the Airbus 320 it operates on the route is not equipped to handle it."
However,the live lobster shipments, weighing 600 to 700 kilos, are to be transported from Marseille to Paris as a bulk load aboard an Air France Europe A320 later today, the official added.
